findings.consequence: Pallet jams at the conveyor entry eye PE-1002 will never be detected. The conveyor motor will continue to drive pallets into the jam, risking mechanical damage, motor overload, and physical damage to EV battery packs.
findings.evidence: Cause-and-effect matrix entry CE-ST10-03 requires that if PE-1002 (X11) is blocked for more than 5.0 s while running, the conveyor motor M-1001 (Y10) must stop and a jam alarm must be raised. Parameter sheet specifies jam_time of 5.0 s on timer T10. Narrative §3 details jam detection intent. Lint check L005 flags X11 as configured in I/O but never referenced. In the program, T10 is never instantiated, X11 is never read, and M190 is evaluated in R3 and reset in R2 but never set anywhere.
findings.proposed_fix: Add rungs to drive timer T10 (K50 for 5.0 s at 100 ms base) when the conveyor motor is running (Y10) and entry photo-eye is blocked (X11): 'LD Y10', 'AND X11', 'OUT T10 K50'. On timer completion, latch M190: 'LD T10', 'SET M190'.
findings.title: Missing conveyor jam detection timer and alarm logic

findings.consequence: The conveyor motor will restart automatically without operator intervention upon thermal reset of the overload relay, violating machinery safety standards (IEC 60204-1) and creating severe entanglement or crushing hazards for technicians inspecting the stalled conveyor.
findings.evidence: R1 drives M191 with an unlatched 'OUT' coil directly from 'LDI X13'. When motor overload MOL-1001 trips, X13 opens (0), setting M191 to 1 and dropping Y10 via M199 in R3 and R4. When the thermal overload relay cools down or auto-resets, contact X13 re-closes (1), de-energizing M191 and clearing M199. R2 provides reset logic only for M190. Because Auto mode selector SS-0003 (X2) remains closed, Y10 immediately re-energizes without operator reset.
findings.proposed_fix: Latch the overload alarm with 'SET M191' when X13 is lost ('LDI X13' -> 'SET M191'). Add reset logic requiring the fault reset pushbutton PB-0002 ('LD X1', 'AND X13', 'RST M191') so the alarm cannot clear until the fault is gone and an operator acknowledges it.
findings.title: Unlatched motor overload alarm permits automatic motor restart after cool-down

findings.consequence: The conveyor restarts motion immediately when the hardwired E-stop safety circuit is re-energized, violating safety standards (ISO 13850 / IEC 60204-1 §9.2.5.4) that require a separate, deliberate manual reset/restart action before hazardous motion resumes.
findings.evidence: In R3, 'ORI X0' is an unlatched branch feeding 'OUT M199'. In R4, 'LD X2' with 'ANI M199' controls 'OUT Y10'. When E-stop healthy contact ES-0001 (X0) drops to 0, M199 turns ON and halts Y10. As soon as the E-stop button is pulled out or the safety relay is reset, X0 returns to 1, immediately dropping M199 to 0. Because Auto mode selector SS-0003 (X2) is a maintained switch, Y10 turns ON immediately without requiring a fault reset or cycle start command.
findings.proposed_fix: Implement a latched fault or run-permissive circuit requiring operator acknowledgement via fault reset pushbutton PB-0002 (X1) after X0 is restored before M199 can clear and allow Y10 to re-energize, while strictly preserving the read of X0 in the stop logic.
findings.title: Automatic conveyor motor restart upon E-stop circuit restoration

findings.consequence: A release request from the line controller while in manual mode or E-stop will energize the solenoid unexpectedly, presenting a pinch point hazard. If triggered when no pallet is at the stop, an incoming pallet may overshoot the test position. If E-stop occurs while the stopper is retracted, Y11 remains held ON in software for the remainder of the 2.0 s timer.
findings.evidence: R6 triggers 'SET Y11' directly from 'LDP X14' without testing Auto mode (X2), E-stop healthy (X0), station fault (M199), or pallet presence at the stop photo-eye (X10 / M100). Furthermore, R8 only resets Y11 upon T11 timer done; neither E-stop nor fault conditions reset Y11 if energized.
findings.proposed_fix: Interlock R6 with Auto mode ('AND X2'), E-stop healthy ('AND X0'), no active fault ('ANI M199'), and pallet at stop confirmed ('AND X10'). Add logic to reset Y11 immediately if E-stop trips or station fault occurs ('LD M199', 'ORI X0', 'RST Y11').
findings.title: Missing operational and safety interlocks on stopper release solenoid XY-1004

findings.consequence: Maintenance technicians and controls engineers cannot readily decipher the roles of internal bits M190 and M199 or actuator Y10 during online troubleshooting, increasing maintenance time and probability of errors.
findings.evidence: Multiple devices used in ST10 logic are absent from <device_comments station="ST10">: M190 (jam alarm), M199 (ST10 common fault), Y10 (M-1001 conveyor motor contactor), X1 (PB-0002 fault reset), X10 (PE-1001 pallet at stop), X13 (MOL-1001 motor overload healthy), and T11 (stopper release pulse timer). Consequently, rungs R1, R2, R3, R4, R5, R7, and R8 lack symbol comments in engineering views.
findings.proposed_fix: Add complete device comments to the project database: M190 'ST10 pallet jam alarm', M199 'ST10 common fault / motor interlock', Y10 'M-1001 conveyor motor contactor', X1 'PB-0002 fault reset pushbutton', X10 'PE-1001 pallet at stop photo-eye', X13 'MOL-1001 conveyor motor overload healthy', and T11 'Stopper release pulse timer'.
findings.title: Missing device comments for critical ST10 internal relays and I/O

data.summary: Engineering review of the ST10 conveyor program identified five defects. Most critically, the entire entry pallet jam detection logic (PE-1002 / X11 and T10 timing for 5.0 s to set M190) is missing, leaving CE-ST10-03 unimplemented. In addition, unlatched fault evaluation allows automatic restart of the conveyor motor upon motor overload cool-down (M191) and upon E-stop chain restoration (X0), violating IEC 60204-1. The stopper release solenoid Y11 lacks basic interlocks against manual mode, E-stop, station fault, and pallet presence, and critical internal relays and I/O lack device comments.
